title: Oscar and the Group Chat
premise: Hazel Kavanagh has survived high school by being useful and invisible—keeping stats for the soccer team, dodging attention, telling herself the school board's 'budget realignment' that gutted the scholarship fund was just paperwork. But when her late grandmother's recipe box yields coded instructions instead of recipes, Hazel discovers her grandmother was part of a secret student network that exposed institutional wrongdoing decades ago—and that the same network's group chat, dormant for years, is pinging again. Following the recipe-box clues with three unlikely allies, Hazel uncovers proof that the board buried a safety scandal to protect donors, and that her grandmother's death may not have been natural. The story ends with Hazel choosing visibility: she publishes the archive at the homecoming assembly, forcing resignations, honoring her grandmother's legacy, and finally accepting that belonging means risking being seen.
about_author: C. M. Yarrow is a former school district archivist who spent years cataloging records no one was supposed to read. They write young adult fiction about quiet kids who find loud ways to matter, and live in a small town with an aggressively opinionated cat.

chapters.title: Fine Is a Full-Time Job
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. We meet her meticulously managed invisible life: stats sheets, lunch in the library, a dead grandmother she hasn't grieved. She notices the scholarship fund quietly vanished from the athletics budget but files it away. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as control; the reader sees how hard 'fine' actually is.

chapters.title: Cardamom, Then Coordinates
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Cleaning out grandma's kitchen, Hazel finds the recipe box—except cards like 'Grief Casserole' contain ciphers, dates, and references to 'the Group Chat.' One card names the school board. Emotional beat: eerie wonder curdling into dread as she realizes grandma left her a case file, not a cookbook.

chapters.title: The Dormant Channel
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with interludes of archived chat logs. She decodes enough to find the old network's messaging channel and posts a test message. To her shock, someone replies: Priya, a senior who inherited her own aunt's connection to the network. Emotional beat: first crack in isolation—the terrifying thrill of being answered.

chapters.title: Three Strangers and a Storage Unit
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya recruits Marcus (a dropout who works nights) and Theo (the editor of the censored school paper). The four break into a storage unit listed on a decoded card, finding boxes of documents from the 1990s network—including a file labeled 'WESTFIELD POOL.' Emotional beat: wary alliance forming over shared purpose.

chapters.title: What the Pool Buried
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The Westfield file reveals the district covered up contaminated water in the old natatorium that sickened students—including, they realize, Hazel's mother. The current board chair's family profited from the demolition contract. Emotional beat: grief becomes fury; the personal stakes snap into focus.

chapters.title: Deniability
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The group tries going through channels: Theo pitches the story, gets killed by the principal; a sympathetic teacher warns them off, scared. Someone photographs them at the storage unit. Emotional beat: the machinery of silence revealed—justice outside the law starts looking like the only justice available.

chapters.title: The Recipe for Ruin
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A final encoded card leads to grandma's safe-deposit box: her investigation notes from 1994, cut short by threats, plus a letter naming a mole inside the original network. Hazel realizes the mole's child now sits on the current board. Emotional beat: heartbreak and resolve—grandma didn't fail, she passed the baton.

chapters.title: Leak Season
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. The group goes on offense: anonymous drops, copied drives, a countdown website tied to homecoming. But the board retaliates—Marcus loses his job, Priya's college recommendation evaporates, and Hazel's mom forbids her to continue, terrified. Emotional beat: rising cost of the fight; the team fractures under pressure.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Climax. At the homecoming assembly, before the board chair speaks, Hazel takes the stage with the archive projected behind her—documents, chat logs, her grandmother's letter. The mole's identity lands like a detonation; phones light up across the gym. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into power; invisibility abandoned mid-sentence.

chapters.title: Everything Is Not Fine (and That's the Point)
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, weeks later. Resignations, a state investigation reopened, the scholarship restored under a new name: the Kavanagh Fund. Hazel grieves her grandmother properly at last, surrounded by friends who saw everything and stayed. Final image: she adds a new card to the recipe box—for whoever inherits it next. Emotional beat: belonging earned, memory honored, justice begun.
